title: Evidence & proof drawer shows '0 events' and empty tabs after a fully completed verified session
user: first-time judge or learner completing the sample
prerequisites: Complete the sample lesson through repair and proof issuance
steps: Start 'Try verified sample' from the homepage
Complete all 6 steps including 'Run the fair test' and 'Verify notebook patch'
On the proof page, click 'Open' on the bottom 'Evidence & proof | 0 events' bar
Click through tabs Activity, Plan, Diff, Tests, Verifier, Provenance
expected: The drawer's tabs list the events the session just produced (test run, verification, diff, capsule issuance), and the counter reflects them.
actual: Header reads '0 events'; Activity/Plan/Diff/Tests/Verifier all show 'No <X> evidence yet. It will appear here when the session produces it.' Only Provenance has rows (artifact hash, session id, result hash).

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: All 5 non-provenance tabs empty after completed session; counter '0 events'

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Provenance tab populated with hashes while sibling tabs are empty

likely_cause: Sample sessions replay pre-computed payloads and never emit runtime proof events to the drawer's event store; empty-state copy is generic and not sample-aware.
unverified: Whether live (uploaded-notebook) sessions populate the drawer; could not upload a file via browser tools.
learner_impact: The product's core promise ('prove it like science') appears broken exactly when the learner finishes; 'It will appear here when the session produces it' wrongly implies pending work.
judge_impact: A judge opening the flagship trust surface on the flagship journey sees an empty console — reads as vaporware.
trust_impact: High negative: the verified narrative is contradicted by the empty evidence UI.
recommended_correction: Emit/synthesize proof events for sample sessions (they exist: plan verification, kernel result, verifier checks, patch, capsule), or make the drawer sample-aware: 'Sample sessions are pre-verified; view the stored chain' with links to proof page sections.
smallest_correction: Change empty-state copy on completed sessions to state that proof lives on the proof page and link to it; fix the '0 events' counter to reflect stored events.
acceptance_criteria: After completing the sample, the drawer shows >=1 item per relevant tab or a clear sample-specific explanation; counter matches visible content.
regression_test: Complete sample session; assert drawer counter > 0 and each tab renders content or a mode-specific explanatory state.

title: Bogus replay id bricks the page: permanent 'Opening this replay…' loader, stale stepper, no recovery CTA
user: any user who mistypes or follows a stale replay link
prerequisites: None (state bleed requires a prior in-progress session in the same browser)
steps: Visit /replay/bogus-id
Observe the error toast and main content
Wait/reload and observe again
expected: A designed 404 state: 'Replay not found', explanation, and a primary action home (or to the replay index); stepper cleared.
actual: Toast pill 'Replay bogus-id was not found' top-right, while the main area shows a permanent 'CHECKING STORED EVIDENCE / Opening this replay…' loading message that never resolves; header still shows 'REPLAY MODE' and the stepper shows stale progress (checkmarks and '3 Test') leaked from the previous session; the only exit is 'START OVER' in the header.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Permanent loader + error toast coexisting; rechecked after waiting — unchanged

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Stepper shows previous session's progress on the error page

likely_cause: Replay loader has no failure branch — fetch error surfaces as toast but the loading view is never replaced; session stepper state is read from local storage regardless of route validity.
unverified: Whether the toast auto-dismisses after a long interval (persisted through my observation window).
judge_impact: A judge probing a bad URL concludes error handling is absent.
trust_impact: Stale 'verified-style' progress on an error page blurs state integrity.
recommended_correction: Add an error branch to the replay loader: full-width 404 card with retry/home actions; reset stepper and mode badge when the replay id is invalid.
smallest_correction: Replace the eternal loader with the toast's message plus a 'Back to start' button when the replay fetch 404s.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown replay id renders a static error screen with a working exit within one second; no stale progress indicators.
regression_test: Visit /replay/does-not-exist; assert error card visible, no 'Opening this replay…' text, stepper has no completed steps.
dependencies: Replay fetch layer; session state store

title: Boundary tab's key statement is ghosted at ~1.6-1.8:1 contrast (effectively unreadable)
user: learner trying to read where the conclusion changes
prerequisites: Run the fair test in the sample session, open the Boundary tab in the Experiment Theater
steps: Complete steps 1-3 of the sample
Run the fair test
Click the 'Boundary' tab inside the Experiment Theater
Read the 'VERIFIED SAMPLE BOUNDARY' card
expected: The boundary statement ('The conclusion changes at the entity boundary.') is rendered at readable contrast (>=4.5:1), visually emphasized as the takeaway of this step.
actual: Heading and body render in light blue-gray on near-white: measured heading 1.82:1, body 1.63:1 (text (167,183,202)/(179,193,213) on (240,242,243)). The most important sentence of the step is the lowest-contrast text in the product; it remains ghosted after full session completion.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Ghosted text confirmed visually with zoom crop

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Pixel-sampled contrast ratios 1.82:1 and 1.63:1

likely_cause: A 'locked/preview' or low-emphasis style applied to the sample boundary card (opacity or muted token) with no state transition to solid after verification.
unverified: Whether a live-session boundary map (interactive) renders at full contrast; sample variant only.
learner_impact: Learners literally cannot read the concept the step exists to teach.
judge_impact: Looks like a rendering bug on a core screen.
trust_impact: A 'VERIFIED SAMPLE BOUNDARY' that cannot be read undermines the verified claim.
recommended_correction: Render the verified boundary statement at full contrast with the same emphasis treatment as other verified outcomes (solid card, statement in display type, overlap numbers as stats).
smallest_correction: Remove the muted/ghost style (opacity or gray token) from the boundary card text.
acceptance_criteria: Boundary statement measures >=4.5:1 contrast and is legible without zoom in the sample journey.
regression_test: Screenshot the Boundary tab in the sample session; assert text/card contrast >=4.5:1.

title: Dark homepage: muted sidebar labels fail WCAG AA (3.07:1 and 2.14:1)
steps: Open the homepage
Inspect sidebar labels 'START WITH EVIDENCE' and 'No account needed'
actual: 'START WITH EVIDENCE' measures 3.07:1 ((92,92,99) on (5,5,6)); 'No account needed' 2.14:1 ((69,69,74) on same); main subtext passes at 4.87:1 but is borderline.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Pixel-sampled contrast ratios

likely_cause: Muted gray tokens chosen for dark theme without contrast checks on the darkest background.
unverified: Exact design-token values (measured from rendered pixels).
learner_impact: Secondary navigation harder to find; accessibility failure.
recommended_correction: Raise muted-label tokens to >=#8A8F98 equivalents on the dark sidebar.
smallest_correction: Lighten the two label classes to meet 4.5:1.
regression_test: Automated a11y contrast scan of / in CI.

title: 'Next:' guidance bar overlaps and clips the content cards on wizard steps
steps: Open step 1 of the sample
Look at the boundary between the 'Next:' bar and the two cards below it
expected: The 'Next:' bar and the cards stack with clear separation; no clipped card titles or hidden borders.
actual: The cards are tucked ~30px underneath the Next bar (negative-margin stacking): the left card's title 'Uploaded notebook evidence' is half-clipped behind the bar; the right card's top corner/border is hidden. Repeats on steps 1-3.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Overlap and clipped title confirmed with zoom crop

likely_cause: Negative top margin on the card grid (or absolute positioning of the Next bar) without z-index/padding compensation.
unverified: Whether intentional 'stacked cards' aesthetic — the clipped title strongly suggests bug.
learner_impact: Sloppy first impression on the very first lesson screen; clipped heading text.
judge_impact: Visible polish bug on the primary journey.
recommended_correction: Remove the negative margin / give the card grid its own top spacing so all card chrome is visible.
smallest_correction: Add margin-top equal to the overlap to the card row, or set the Next bar position static in flow.
acceptance_criteria: No card content or border is obscured at 100% zoom on any wizard step.
regression_test: Visual snapshot of step 1 asserting the left card title is fully visible.

title: Verified notebook diff renders without any +/- color coding (all lines uniform gray)
user: learner or judge inspecting the verified change
prerequisites: Complete the sample session; open 'See the verified notebook change'
steps: Finish the sample
On the proof page expand 'See the verified notebook change'
Inspect the diff lines
expected: Removed lines red-tinted, added lines green-tinted (background and/or text), hunk headers visually distinct — the universal diff affordance.
actual: '-from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split', '+from sklearn.model_selection import GroupShuffleSplit', context lines and '@@' hunk headers all render in the same gray-white mono on navy; only the leading -/+ glyphs distinguish them.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Uniform color confirmed by zoomed crop and pixel sampling

likely_cause: Diff rendered as plain preformatted text without per-line classes for additions/deletions.
unverified: Whether syntax highlighting was intended and failed, or never implemented.
learner_impact: The repair payoff ('what exactly changed in my notebook') is harder to parse; the pedagogical punch of the patch is muted.
judge_impact: Reads as an unfinished detail on the product's proof surface.
trust_impact: Moderate: the 'verified change' should be scannable at a glance.
recommended_correction: Add per-line addition/deletion styling (tinted backgrounds + colored glyphs), keep monospace, add subtle line numbers if space allows.
smallest_correction: Color - lines #f87171-ish and + lines #34d399-ish (or tinted row backgrounds) based on the leading glyph.
acceptance_criteria: Added and removed lines are distinguishable by color alone in a screenshot.
regression_test: Visual snapshot of the proof diff asserting distinct classes/colors for + and - rows.

title: Live flow without an uploaded artifact enters a permanent false-loading state ('Preparing artifact…', red LOADING pill)
user: learner who clicks 'Continue with my notebook' before choosing a file
prerequisites: Visit /new and click 'Continue with my notebook' without selecting a file
steps: Open /new
Click 'Continue with my notebook'
Observe the evidence card state and the disabled CTA
expected: Either the file picker is required before entering the step, or the step shows an explicit empty state ('No notebook yet — upload one') with the upload control emphasized.
actual: The evidence card shows a red 'LOADING' pill, 'Preparing artifact…', 'Not available' metric, and integrity 'Pending intake / 0 cells / Pending' indefinitely; nothing is actually loading; the disabled 'Compare two explanations' button gives no reason. Red (an error color) is used for a loading badge.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: False-loading state persisted through the session; starter-claim fill works but CTA stays disabled

likely_cause: Artifact state machine lacks a distinct 'absent' state and defaults to the loading presentation; entry is not gated on file selection.
unverified: Behaviour after a real upload (file dialog not available to browser tools).
learner_impact: Confusing dead-end; the app pretends to be working when it is waiting for the user.
judge_impact: A judge poking the live path sees a hung-looking screen.
trust_impact: Moderate: fake loading erodes trust in real loading states elsewhere.
recommended_correction: Gate entry on file selection (open the picker on 'Continue'), and add an explicit 'No notebook yet' empty state; reserve LOADING for actual intake and use a neutral color.
smallest_correction: When no artifact exists, swap 'Preparing artifact…' for 'No notebook yet — choose one below' and hide the LOADING pill.
acceptance_criteria: No indefinite loading copy is shown when no upload is in progress; the CTA's disabled reason is stated.
regression_test: Enter /new without a file; assert empty-state copy appears and no LOADING badge renders.

title: Falsification reveal fires instantly with no staged transition; the drop is not visually encoded (no chart, no color direction)
prerequisites: Seal a prediction and click 'Run the fair test'
steps: Click 'Run the fair test'
Observe the transition into the Experiment Theater
expected: A brief staged beat (e.g., 'Running fixed kernel…' -> theater fades in), and a visual encoding of 98.5% vs 59.4% (paired bars or directional color) so the magnitude of the collapse is grasped in under a second.
actual: The screenshot taken immediately after the click already shows the fully settled theater (instant swap, no observed suspense state); both numerals render at identical size and color with only a thin teal arrow between them; no chart exists anywhere in the product for this comparison.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Settled theater visible immediately post-click

evidence.label: Inferred from behaviour
evidence.detail: No intermediate/animating state observed across the click boundary (static captures)

likely_cause: Sample result is pre-computed so the UI skips any pending state; the theater design is typographic rather than chart-based.
unverified: Sub-300ms animations cannot be confirmed from static screenshots.
learner_impact: The emotional peak of the lesson passes without ceremony; magnitude of the drop requires reading, not seeing.
judge_impact: The 'wow' moment under-delivers relative to the copy's ambition.
trust_impact: Neutral-positive currently; a staged verification beat would increase perceived rigor.
recommended_correction: Add a short verification beat (kernel run status, ~1-2s or skippable) before the theater; add a minimal two-bar comparison visual with the group bar visually diminished.
smallest_correction: Add a paired horizontal-bar graphic (98.5 vs 59.4) inside the theater, and a 400-800ms fade/scale-in on the theater.
acceptance_criteria: A visible transition state exists between 'Run the fair test' and the settled theater; the two results are distinguishable graphically, not only numerically.
regression_test: Capture frames across the click; assert an intermediate state and a chart element in the theater.

title: Disabled primary buttons are washed-out low-contrast and give no reason for being disabled
user: any user blocked by a form gate
steps: Open homepage with empty textarea (or live step without artifact)
Inspect the disabled CTA
expected: Disabled state remains legible and, where the gate is non-obvious, explains what is missing (tooltip or inline hint).
actual: Homepage disabled CTA measures 2.52:1 (text (36,44,62) on (87,104,145)); wizard disabled CTA is white text on very light blue; neither explains the gate (empty claim / missing notebook).

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Pixel-measured 2.52:1 on homepage; visual check on wizard

likely_cause: Single low-opacity disabled token; no gating-reason messaging pattern.
unverified: Tooltip-on-hover for disabled buttons (no hover tool).
learner_impact: Users may not understand why they cannot proceed.
recommended_correction: Darken disabled tokens to ~3:1 minimum and add inline gate reasons ('Enter a claim to continue', 'Upload a notebook first').
smallest_correction: Add a one-line reason under disabled CTAs on gated steps.
acceptance_criteria: Every gated CTA states its gate; disabled text >=3:1.
regression_test: Snapshot disabled CTA states; assert presence of reason text.

title: Native unstyled file input ('Choose File / No file chosen') clashes with the custom design system
steps: Scroll to 'Use a different notebook' on step 1
expected: A styled upload control matching the product's buttons/dropzones.
actual: Browser-default gray 'Choose File' button and 'No file chosen' text sit inside an otherwise fully custom card.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Native control visible in the upload area

recommended_correction: Style the upload as a dropzone/button consistent with the design system.
smallest_correction: Visually hide the native input and trigger it from a styled button with chosen-file name display.
acceptance_criteria: No browser-default chrome visible in the upload area.
regression_test: Visual snapshot of step 1 upload area.

title: Rule-builder clause <select> controls truncate their option text ('rows repeat the s…')
prerequisites: Reach the Apply tab in the Experiment Theater
steps: Inspect the When / I should / because clause dropdowns
expected: Each clause control shows its full selected clause (or wraps it).
actual: Three narrow selects truncate every clause to ~15 characters; the learner cannot read the full clause in the control (full text only reappears in the composed sentence below).

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Truncated select values visible

likely_cause: Three-column grid forces ~200px-wide native selects with ellipsis truncation.
learner_impact: Mild comprehension friction during the reflection task.
recommended_correction: Replace native selects with custom wrapping option cards, or stack the three clauses vertically at readable width.
smallest_correction: Widen columns to two-row layout so selects fit ~30 characters.
acceptance_criteria: Full clause text visible in each control after selection.
regression_test: Visual snapshot of the Apply tab with selections made.

title: Sidebar 'How proof works' link has no visible destination or action
steps: Click 'How proof works' in the homepage sidebar
expected: Navigation to a proof-explainer view (or opening a modal).
actual: URL stays on '/'; only the sidebar hover/active background changes; the page already shows a short 'How proof works:' blurb, so nothing perceptible happens.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: No navigation or content change after click

likely_cause: Anchor with missing/self href, or an unfinished route.
unverified: Whether an in-page scroll was intended (page fits viewport, so none occurs).
judge_impact: Dead link on the first screen.
recommended_correction: Point it at a real destination (e.g., the /judge proof section or a dedicated explainer).
smallest_correction: Link it to /judge#proof or remove it.
acceptance_criteria: Click produces a visible, meaningful result.
regression_test: Click the link; assert URL or DOM change.

title: Provenance rows read as statuses but go stale ('Boundary: Locked until verification' after verification completed)
prerequisites: Complete the sample session; open drawer Provenance tab
steps: Finish sample
Open Evidence & proof drawer
Click Provenance
expected: Statuses reflect the completed state ('Boundary: Verified', 'Capsule: Issued').
actual: 'Boundary: Locked until verification' is shown after verification and repair completed; 'Capsule: Issued after verified repair' is phrased as policy, leaving the actual issuance state ambiguous.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Stale/ambiguous provenance rows on completed session

likely_cause: Rows are static descriptors rather than bound to session state.
unverified: Whether 'Boundary' here refers to a separate Boundary Map feature that is genuinely still locked in sample mode.
learner_impact: Minor confusion about what is actually verified.
judge_impact: Moderate: provenance is a trust surface and its states contradict the journey.
recommended_correction: Bind provenance rows to session state with explicit current values and timestamps.
smallest_correction: Reword rows as static facts ('Boundary check: verified on whole-customer split') or mark policy rows distinctly from state rows.
acceptance_criteria: No provenance row contradicts the session's completed state.
regression_test: Complete sample; assert provenance rows show verified/issued states.

title: Two disconnected visual languages: dark chat homepage vs light editorial app/dossier
user: every user crossing from home into the lesson
steps: Open /
Then open /judge or start the sample
Compare typography, color, and component language
expected: A bridged system: shared tokens/type so the chat entry and the lesson feel like one product.
actual: Homepage is near-black, sans-only, chat-app chrome (sidebar + textarea, like ChatGPT/Claude); every other surface is cream paper with serif display type and dossier/editorial chrome. No shared element except the logo and the navy accent; the transition between them is a hard cut.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Dark chat home vs light editorial wizard and dossier

likely_cause: Two design phases (chat entry bolted onto an editorial lesson product) without a unifying token layer.
unverified: Whether the split is a deliberate 'ask in chat, prove in print' concept; even so, no visual bridge exists.
learner_impact: Mild disorientation at the entry boundary.
judge_impact: Product feels like two demos stitched together; weakens 'coherent new category' claim.
recommended_correction: Introduce shared tokens (bring the serif + cream into at least the homepage hero, or carry dark surfaces and lavender accents into a dark variant of the wizard header) so one design system spans both modes.
smallest_correction: Restyle the homepage hero headline in the editorial serif and add the cream/mint accents used elsewhere (or vice versa: give the wizard header a dark mode echo of the home sidebar).
acceptance_criteria: A screenshot pair of / and /session shares identifiable typography and color tokens.
regression_test: Visual comparison checklist across the two surfaces in design review.

title: No charts anywhere: the 98.5% -> 59.4% collapse is purely typographic
steps: Inspect the reveal panel and the judge dossier hero card
expected: At least one minimal graphical comparison (paired bars) supporting the numerals.
actual: All quantitative results are numerals and tables only (theater numerals, metrics table, dossier card); no bar/line/visual encoding of the central comparison exists in the product.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Numerals-only presentation in theater, table, and dossier

likely_cause: Typographic design choice; charting never added.
learner_impact: Magnitude of the collapse requires arithmetic, not perception; weaker for visual learners.
judge_impact: Missed opportunity on the headline number pair.
recommended_correction: Add a two-bar (or slope) graphic in the theater and dossier card with accessible labels.
smallest_correction: CSS-only paired bars under the numerals.
acceptance_criteria: The 98.5 vs 59.4 comparison is perceivable graphically.
regression_test: Visual snapshot of the theater containing the graphic.

title: /new readiness screen shows stepper at 'Step 1 of 6 Question' before the lesson has started
steps: Open /new and observe the header stepper
expected: Stepper is hidden, or shows a 'Setup' state, while content is a pre-lesson readiness check.
actual: Stepper displays '1 Question' active although no question/session exists yet.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Active Question step on the readiness screen

likely_cause: Stepper bound to route-level step default rather than session state.
learner_impact: Minor; implies progress that does not exist.
recommended_correction: Show a 'Setup' pill or dim the stepper until the session is created.
smallest_correction: Render the stepper in an all-inactive state on /new.
acceptance_criteria: No step appears active before the session exists.
regression_test: Snapshot /new; assert no active step styling.

title: Reveal numerals lack directional encoding (98.5% and 59.4% identical size/color; only a thin teal arrow)
steps: Inspect the big comparison row in the theater
expected: The regression is encoded visually (e.g., diminished/red-tinted new-customer numeral, down arrow, or delta badge '-39.1 pts').
actual: Both numerals share size and color; direction is carried by a small teal arrow and the caption sentence; no delta or directional styling.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Uniform numeral styling

likely_cause: Deliberate neutral/scientific styling (avoid red-alarm framing) without a compensating delta display.
learner_impact: Weaker instant comprehension of 'it fell by 39 points'.
recommended_correction: Add a delta chip ('-39.1 points on unseen customers') and directional arrow styling; keep numerals neutral if red is off-brand.
smallest_correction: Add the delta chip between the numerals.
acceptance_criteria: The magnitude and direction of change are visible without reading body copy.
regression_test: Visual snapshot of the theater containing the delta indicator.

title: Transient blue focus-outline box around the homepage H1 on first paint
steps: Load the homepage fresh and observe the headline
expected: No visible focus ring on a non-interactive heading.
actual: First capture shows a bright blue rectangular outline around the H1 'What result are you trying to understand?'; subsequent visits/interactions do not show it.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Outline present on first capture, absent later

evidence.label: Inferred from behaviour
evidence.detail: Consistent with autofocus/programmatic focus on mount (or automation-induced focus)

likely_cause: Focus() call on the heading (a11y focus management) or automation focus artifact.
unverified: Whether real users (non-automation) see it; could not confirm without DevTools.
recommended_correction: Use focus-visible semantics so programmatic focus on a heading does not paint a ring.
smallest_correction: Remove tabindex/focus call from the H1, or add :focus-visible-only styling.
acceptance_criteria: No outline on the H1 at first paint in a real browser.
